sites.name: H & H INC., BURN PIT

portals.name: Hanover County Parcel Search and Mapping Application
portals.note: The county page says assessed values can be found through this application by subdivision, parcel ID, mailing address or property address. The page does not say whether an account or fee is required. Not opened directly.

portals.name: Hanover County Circuit Court Clerk, Deeds & Plats Self Service (Land Title Research)
portals.note: The page says Self Service gives free access to indexes only. Document copies may be purchased. A separate paid Secure Remote Access subscription gives document images at $500 per year or $50 per month. Index search was not run for this site.

facts.summary: EPA's site profile describes the one-acre H & H Inc. Burn Pit Superfund site as located in Hanover County, Virginia. The page gives no date for this description.
facts.reference: EPA site profile, H & H Inc., Burn Pit (site id 0302659)
facts.quote: The one-acre H & H Inc., Burn Pit Superfund site is located in Hanover County, Virginia.

facts.summary: EPA's profile says Haskell Chemical Company of Richmond used the site for disposal from 1960 to 1976. The page gives no date for this history beyond those years.
facts.reference: EPA site profile, H & H Inc., Burn Pit (site id 0302659)
facts.quote: Between 1960 and 1976, Haskell Chemical Company, located in Richmond, Virginia, used the area

facts.summary: EPA's profile says the institutional controls at the site consist of a restrictive covenant on the property deed that prevents use of the contaminated groundwater under the property. The page gives no recording date for the covenant.
facts.reference: EPA site profile, H & H Inc., Burn Pit (site id 0302659), second cleanup page
facts.quote: These institutional controls have been implemented and consist of a restrictive covenant on the property deed

facts.summary: EPA issued an amendment to the Record of Decision for the site in May 2020. It modifies the Operable Unit 2 groundwater remedy to use enhanced bioremediation.
facts.reference: EPA Record of Decision amendment, H & H Inc. Burn Pit (May 2020)
facts.quote: In May 2020, EPA issued an amendment to the Record of Decision (ROD) for the H&H Inc. Burn Pit Superfund Site.

facts.summary: EPA's profile says the site owners operate a timber lot at the site. The owners are not named on the page, and the page gives no date for this use.
facts.reference: EPA site profile, H & H Inc., Burn Pit (site id 0302659), second cleanup page
facts.quote: The site owners operate a timber lot at the site.

facts.summary: EPA's profile says the next five-year review will be conducted in 2030.
facts.reference: EPA site profile, H & H Inc., Burn Pit (site id 0302659), second cleanup page
facts.quote: The next five-year review will be conducted in 2030.

gaps: No owner of record was established. EPA says only 'the site owners' and the atlas owner is null. A deed search in the Hanover clerk index is needed to name them.

An EPA ROD amendment excerpt from a search result gives parcel 7748-68-4801 and says an environmental covenant was filed with the county clerk on December 20, 2010 at Book 2992, Page 1438. The PDF text could not be extracted, so these were not recorded as facts. They are the first things to check in the Hanover clerk index and the parcel map.
The Hanover parcel search was not run. The atlas address (10 MILES N RTE 33) is not a usable street address, and the parcel id in the atlas is null.
It is not established whether the 2010 covenant remains in force or was amended, because no clerk record was opened.
EPA's profile says the fifth five-year review was recently completed, but gives no date. The 2017 EPA reuse page in a search result predates the current status and was not used.
The NPL listing year (1989 in a search excerpt) was not confirmed on an opened page, so it is not recorded as a fact.
No tax delinquency, lien, permit, code-enforcement or zoning record was searched. Hanover's paid Secure Remote Access was not used.
